gen-fs-quilon-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Tight, warm, quietly rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its tall lowercase close, with curves that never quite shut. Quilon is the one that flexes, swelling gently in its stroke; Pilcrow stays level.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-ranade: Quilon swells and thins in a slow, editorial rhythm. Ranade, spaced wide and shifting only slightly in weight, gives the pair its strongest quality: a headline with presence over text that breathes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa is a text serif with tall, sturdy lowercase and counters that spill generously into the space around them. And Quilon above it keeps the editorial tone going with its own gentle swell of stroke.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-savate: Editorial and commanding, Quilon swells and thins calmly across large open counters, while Savate lays down sturdy hairlines and open jaws. That plain sans keeps text feeling clean and contemporary throughout.
gen-fs-quilon-instrument-sans: Commanding and editorial, Quilon varies its stroke with a measured thick-thin ratio, while Instrument Sans looks cut from strips of equal width. Paragraphs in the plain sans come across clean and modern.
gen-fs-rajdhani-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One slows the eye to a leisurely walk, all curvy and authoritative. Rajdhani's dense, tightly woven strips make a brisker contrast, so a slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-fs-rajdhani-newsreader: Authoritative is the mood Newsreader gives the body, while Rajdhani above it stays clean and modern with tightly woven lines. Newsreader then carries a long page as a text serif with restrained stress and open jaws on its curves.
gen-fs-rajdhani-source-serif-4: Dignified and a touch stern, Source Serif 4 tightens its strokes slightly at the tops of curves and leaves a gaping c. And Rajdhani's marker-tip letters sit above it, modern where the serif is letterpress-minded.
gen-fs-ranade-fs-karma: Ranade leads with friendly, widely tracked lowercase that looks bigger than its capitals. Karma, a text serif with a very small gap between x-height and cap height, can go up a size to hold its own.
gen-fs-ranade-gf-graduate: Graduate reads dignified and bookish, with generous white between letters and an unshaded, steady outline. But Ranade is the friendlier one, its mild taper like wire rolled barely flat, while Graduate does its best work holding a line.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-archivo: Bold marker lines up top, a commanding body below. Red Hat Display does best at confident, constant-width lines with daylight in every curve, while Archivo does best at outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-clash-grotesk: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws with a marker's constant width. Clash Grotesk, a sans-serif, drops stroke modulation entirely, so its clean, approachable lines sit beside the heading's visible daylight without competing.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-alpino: Alpino reads cozy and a bit squat, its tall body making ascenders look short. Red Hat Display handles the smooth, plotter-like heading work, and Alpino keeps the casual text feeling snug with curve endings held well apart.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-karma: Red Hat Display moves with a skimming ease, its stroke never changing weight. Karma's text serif then settles in with a mild, letterpress-like modulation and terminals clear of the stem, so a long passage feels trustworthy.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-literata: Red Hat Display keeps one line width through every curve and straight, like a marker on paper. Literata serif is the bookish counterpart, with thin strokes only slightly slimmer than its stems.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-merriweather-s: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, with an e that opens clearly rightward. And paragraphs settle into a sturdy, unhurried rhythm under the marker-like lines of Red Hat Display.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-roundo: Roundo reads geometric and tidy, its n built with arch and stem matching. Red Hat Display is the bolder voice, with a marker-like line and open curves, while the sans-serif body keeps every small counter unclogged.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-carme: Carme reads modern and open, its counters leading outward. Beneath the bold marker lines of Red Hat Display, whole paragraphs of its spaghetti-like line travel smoothly across the page.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-domine: Red Hat Display bends each letter like a single wire. It earns its keep big and brief, while Domine serif adds dignity with tall lowercase and a tempered contrast.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-faculty-glyphi: Faculty Glyphic reads low and soft, a plain sans with rounded openings. Red Hat Display draws wire-cut strokes that hold up in big sizes, while the body font is happiest in running text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-judson: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws one marker-like line with daylight in every curve. Judson, dignified and bookish, brings brush-lifted curve ends and fine hairlines, so extended reading feels settled and deliberate.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-snippet: Red Hat Display draws everything with a marker's constant width, leaving visible daylight inside every curve. But Snippet's wire-bent words and crescent-wrench c add a quirky, approachable streak beneath the bold heading.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-instrument-sans: Red Hat Display holds one marker-like width throughout, with visible daylight inside every curve. And Instrument Sans, with its pincer-open c and unvarying stroke, gives paragraphs a clean, modern, steady pace.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-montserrat: Red Hat Display draws a marker-steady line with daylight inside every curve. Montserrat brings the real surprise: generous white space, oversized counters and a wire-smooth glide that make the pairing feel inviting.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-newsreader: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws every stroke like a marker line, with daylight inside each curve. Newsreader, a serif, keeps its stems and hairlines close, so paragraphs flow smoothly.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-nunito-sans: Bold, hairline-free letters up top, soft open-mouthed curves below: Red Hat Display sits over a low, gentle Nunito Sans. Give the heading a generous size and let the sans-serif text stay modest.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-outfit: Red Hat Display draws a marker-like line, contemporary and bold, with visible daylight inside every curve. Outfit follows with curves that finish before they close, cable-bent and unswelling, and that is the strongest quality of this sans-serif pair.
gen-fs-rosaline-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans sets soft, open-mouthed curves in small letters, quiet and neutral. And Rosaline, a flowing pen-written script with closed, sharp-edged forms, gives a handful of lines a luxurious lift above that sans-serif.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-paquito: Paquito reads low and confident, a serif with hardly any gap between lowercase and caps. RX100 crowds its twine-like strokes into a futuristic, compact run, while Paquito is the one for a handful of lines of text.
gen-fs-segment-fs-alpino: Segment spaces its letters wide and stands tall in the middle, with counters that breathe. Alpino, a cozy sans, sits tight and compact beneath it, so the heading looks grand and the text looks handy.
gen-fs-segment-montserrat: Segment leaves wide gaps between its letters and stacks a stocky, tall middle band into every line, which feels commanding. Montserrat glides smoothly beneath it, a good fit for brief reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-chillax: Expressive and bold, Sharpie crowds its letters behind what feels like a narrow slot. Chillax loosens things with open, relaxed curves that never thin at the turns, and it is made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters that feel trustworthy at a glance. Over a longer stretch it would read steadily, while Sharpie keeps its tight, hairline-gapped letters up top.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-rowan: Sharpie packs bold, expressive letters behind a hairline-thin gap, while Rowan's friendly text serif keeps every curve open. Save Sharpie for big, brief headings, and let Rowan stay in light doses.
gen-fs-spline-sans-fs-literata: Rounded, nib-like strokes with no swelling at their ends give Spline Sans an approachable, geometric look. And Literata, a bookish text serif with sturdy hairlines and wide-mouthed curves, would carry a longer stretch of reading with a quiet, sophisticated pull.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-asap: Dramatic lowercase in outsized proportions, Stardom sets thick diagonals against hairline counter-strokes for a showy look. And Asap, readable with open-arc c forms, carries a brief stretch of text without fuss.
gen-fs-styro-fs-alpino: Alpino has open, casual curves with endings kept well apart. Styro, by contrast, presses its letters together into a crowded, retro block, so it is better for brief copy than for pages of text.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space around each curve. Styro delivers crowded, retro punch from a sizable lowercase, while Bespoke Sans handles the finer, more open lines.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab is a grounded, refined serif with tall bodies in every lowercase letter, not meant for long paragraphs. Bespoke Slab gets modest sizing, and Styro supplies the retro, commanding heading above it.
gen-fs-styro-fs-hoover: Retro and crowded, with letters pressed shoulder to shoulder. Styro's tight, closed shapes get relief from Hoover, a serif whose open e eyes and short ascenders keep brief text refined.
gen-fs-styro-fs-nunito: Nunito reads soft and friendly, with big round bowls and stroke ends that finish away from the stem. And the tension is the draw: Styro's closed, crowded letters against Nunito's open ones, though neither suits long paragraphs.
gen-fs-styro-fs-quicksand: Styro presses its lowercase so tight that the counters nearly shut, a retro, commanding look. Quicksand, a sans of tubular strokes and tall glassy bowls, opens everything Styro closes, which is best for quick lines.
gen-fs-styro-fs-ranade: Styro is retro and commanding, crowding its large lowercase until the counters barely open. And Ranade, a sans with widely spaced letters and a faint watercolor shift in weight, does the breathing Styro cannot.
gen-fs-styro-fs-technor: Technor reads like neon tube, cool and geometric, with one steady line thickness and a wide channel into every bowl. Styro's crowded retro punch is the hook, and best taken in sips.
gen-fs-styro-general-sans: Styro packs its big lowercase so tightly the eyes of its letters almost close, loud and retro. General Sans handles the quiet work, drawing smooth open bends at a steady pressure while Styro takes the commanding lines.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One reads big and round, with a very large lowercase eye and letters hung out like clothespins on a line. Styro's crowded, closed letters make the sharpest difference of all.
gen-fs-styro-gf-prompt: Styro brings retro command, its lowercase large and its letters pressed together until the openings nearly vanish. But Prompt, with oversized small letters and open apertures, feels like a window thrown wide beside it.
gen-fs-styro-instrument-sans: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its letters until the counters almost close up. Instrument Sans would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly, its c ends pointing apart like pincers and its strokes never varying.
gen-fs-supreme-fs-erode: Erode brings editorial dignity with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. What stands out most is Supreme's tall, understated sans-serif lowercase, which gives each curve room against Erode's serif texture.
gen-fs-synonym-fs-literata: Synonym draws its small curves wide open, with joins as slim as a pipe cleaner and no flaring at the stroke ends. Literata, a classic serif, is bookish by comparison, its thin and thick lines only gently different.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-karma: Tanker turns every open curve inward, packing heavy letters with barely any gaps between them. And Karma, a serif, lets its terminals finish clear of the stem, so it carries the quieter reading while Tanker keeps to brief copy.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-graduate: Tanker hits heavy and commanding, its curves turning inward and its letters packed tight, while Graduate gives dignified, bookish letters room. Paragraphs in Graduate would move slowly and steadily, every stem alike.
gen-fs-tanker-montserrat: Heavy and commanding, Tanker packs its big lowercase tight. Montserrat has oversized e and a counters and a wire-like glide, so it handles a handful of lines while Tanker leads.
gen-fs-teko-fs-bespoke-sans: Tightly packed letters cut from strokes like bent steel rod. What stands out most is how Teko's rigid, uniform line meets the sharper, more open curves of Bespoke Sans.
gen-fs-teko-fs-karma: Teko sets tightly packed letters in strokes like bent steel rod, with no hairlines and no shadows anywhere. Karma, a classic serif, handles the quieter work with moderate contrast.
gen-fs-teko-gf-graduate: Confident from the first glance, Teko packs its steel-rod strokes together with almost no gaps, while Graduate, a serif, spaces its letters out generously. Bold meets bookish here, tight against loose, and neither backs down.
gen-fs-telma-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, a tall-bodied sans with curve endings kept apart, though lengthy paragraphs aren't its job. Telma's graceful, pen-written script is happiest when big and brief.
gen-fs-telma-fs-familjen-grotesk: Telma flows in a graceful, understated script with a high mean line. The standout is how Telma's gradual stroke swells meet Familjen Grotesk's lively, open-sided bowls, in text made for brief reading.
gen-fs-telma-fs-hoover: Hoover is a sturdy text serif with compressed ascenders. With Telma writing the headline in flowing script, this body keeps the reading smooth, best when the text stays brief.
gen-fs-telma-fs-karma: Karma reads trustworthy and classic, its terminals finishing well away from the stem and its modulation never snagging the eye. Pen-written Telma gives it a graceful partner, best for brief text.
gen-fs-telma-fs-paquito: Paquito is a confident, approachable text serif with capitals barely taller than its lowercase, placed under Telma. Text flows comfortably across the page, though a few lines suit it best.
gen-fs-telma-montserrat: Telma writes graceful pen-made letters with a high mean line and a wide-mouthed a. And Montserrat glides beneath it, its oversized counters keeping the text pleasant in modest amounts.
gen-fs-trench-slab-archivo: Big, burly and unmistakably industrial, thanks to those outsized lowercase proportions. Trench Slab handles loud presence best, while Archivo does the quiet editorial work, with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-fs-trench-slab-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro takes the body, with strokes like bent steel rod and a mean line set high, clean and neutral. And Trench Slab, industrial and oversized in the lowercase, gives the pair its loudest quality.
gen-fs-trench-slab-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its round open letters holding up even at small sizes. Rubik's big lowercase beside capitals is the pair's strongest quality, and it gives Trench Slab's industrial slabs room to stand out.
gen-fs-zina-clash-grotesk: Zina draws fat downstrokes against threadlike upstrokes, giving its spacing a wide-toothed, striking look. But Clash Grotesk never swells in its bowls, a plain foil, happiest when the text stays brief.
gen-fs-zina-fs-literata: Sharp-edged display drama, then a bookish body that opens up. Zina keeps its letters closed and dramatic, Literata lets its curves stand wide, and that shift from tight to open is the real hook.
gen-fs-zina-fs-roundo: Striking and refined, Zina swings from fat downstrokes to threadlike upstrokes. Zina handles the showy moments with closed, wide-set letters, while Roundo's geometric sans-serif keeps small counters open for brief reading.
gen-fs-zina-fs-rowan: Sharp-edged and dramatic, Zina snaps from thick to hairline within each letter. Rowan's strongest quality is the gradual, friendly weight change in its open serif curves, though it is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-zina-fs-sentient: Ultra-fine hairlines crash into heavy strokes, and the effect is striking. Sentient, a pinched, measured text serif, steadies the page beneath Zina, best kept to modest amounts of reading.
gen-fs-zina-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One reads slowly and curvily, thin joins as sturdy as its stems, like a leisurely walk. Zina is the sharper foil above it, so a long passage would feel unhurried, with dark strokes giving way to hairlines.
gen-fugaz-one-fs-rowan: Fugaz One looks like a bent paperclip, all narrow margins and no swelling. Rowan, a literary text serif whose curves open generously, reads warmly line after line, though it isn't built for lengthy paragraphs.
gen-general-sans-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified and editorial, its stroke weights shifting just enough to be noticed. General Sans does the crisp, constant-width headline work best, while Erode handles the broad-mouthed running text.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-general-sans: General Sans draws every letter with one steady nib, smooth around each bend. General Sans sits beside Abyssinica SIL, whose short ascenders, big bowls and gentle contrast give the serif a dignified feel.
gen-gf-amiri-quran-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and bookish, Amiri Quran leads with gently shaded strokes. It excels at dense, knitted strands of touching letters, while Bespoke Sans is best at sharp, refined shapes with generous space where curves meet stems.
gen-gf-arbutus-general-sans: Arbutus is classic and dignified, its big counters and far-apart letters giving the serif a friendly, mild contrast. And General Sans moves along smoothly, its steady pen pressure and filled-out x-height keeping paragraphs easy to follow.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-alpino: Expressive, with a laser-etched trace running through every letter of Autour One. Alpino does the quieter job, a cozy, casual sans whose tall body makes ascenders look short and keeps curve endings well apart.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-paquito: Autour One is bold and expressive, with clear channels leading into each round letter. Then Paquito, a confident serif with caps sitting close to the lowercase, brings an approachable tone that softens the display punch.
gen-gf-autour-one-fs-ranade: Autour One is bold and expressive, drawn with no hairline-to-stem shift at all. Its strongest quality is the flat, uniform stroke, which Ranade, a sans with slight rubber-cord shading and widely spaced type, softens beautifully.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-atkinson-hyperlegib: Bold, open rounds: Autour One keeps every stroke free of calligraphic swell. Beneath it, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next brings approachable sans-serif lowercase with big open eyes, so text stays clear under the loud heading.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-montserrat-alternat: Autour One hits hard, all round shapes and no hairline shifts. What ties them is a uniform line: Montserrat Alternates matches its round rims to its stems, and its lowercase crowds up toward cap height.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Neon-tube lines, bold and showy: Autour One keeps every stroke uniform while the shapes stay round. Noto Sans Syriac then adds tall, bulb-like bowls to soften the handoff.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-serif-grantha: Refined, mostly: Noto Serif Grantha keeps modest stress in its curves and oversized-looking small letters. But Autour One's talent is pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin, loud where Grantha is measured.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-fs-karma: Expressive and flat-lined, Balsamiq Sans keeps a single weight and never pinches a curve. Karma is the opposite, a trustworthy text face with a gentle pencil-like taper and terminals that stop short of the stem.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-actor: Flat, chunky, and cheerfully loud from edge to edge. Balsamiq Sans does the single-weight shout best, while Actor handles the quieter work, with wide s curves barely curled in.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-sour-gummy: Loud, bold, and entirely free of calligraphic shading. Balsamiq Sans is at its best making a statement, while Sour Gummy, a modern sans, keeps tiny sizes crisp through wide gaps.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-spectral: Spectral draws its stems a touch heavier than its crossbars, with the gentle thinning of letters stamped in soft metal. But Balsamiq Sans is the better shouter, a monoline heading that never varies.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-rowan: Distinctive: Baumans draws a c like a crescent wrench opened wide. Rowan, a friendly serif, adds gentle variation in line weight inside each letter, so the uniform heading gets a softer follow-up.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-actor: Baumans hits hard, its crescent-wrench c opened wide and every stroke uniform. Actor takes over below, its sans-serif s curves wide and barely curled in, a quieter partner for the stout heading.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-cardo: Baumans has a c like a crescent wrench and strokes like drawn wire. Cardo supplies the literary counterweight, its fuller stems and slimmer links making a soft cadence under all that uniform wire.

gen-gf-baumans-gf-mate: Mate reads soft and cupped, its round letters never clenched. Mate's gentle step from heavy to light strokes carries a long page along smoothly, while Baumans keeps its marker-plain heading firmly above.

gen-gf-baumans-plus-jakarta-sans: Blunt, crescent-wrench energy up top, with Baumans stamping every stroke at a single thickness. Plus Jakarta Sans then carries the text in precise monoline strokes whose curve endings stay well apart, so paragraphs read smoothly.
gen-gf-baumans-sora: Sora reads crisp and geometric, with its c and s kept widely parted and no swelling at the curves. Baumans is best at commanding attention with its uniform, wrench-open lettering, and Sora is best at quietly carrying the details.
gen-gf-bellota-author: Author brings a refined, dignified voice, with just a slight swell on its bowls. Author handles the steady reading in a classic serif, while Bellota is best at making a flat, stylus-width statement with far-hanging s ends.

gen-gf-bellota-fs-roundo: Distinctive, and a little commanding too, thanks to Bellota's far-reaching s. Roundo's sans keeps every small counter unclogged and its n tidy, which makes the pairing's strongest quality a crisp, geometric clarity.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-rowan: Rowan is literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve. Bellota draws every line flat and unmodulated above, while Rowan below adds a mild swing between heavy and light strokes.

gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sour-gummy: Sour Gummy reads modern and crisp, with wide gaps that hold up small. Under Bellota Text, with its marker-drawn plainness and commanding presence, a long page would feel steady and unhurried.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-spectral: A wire-like line gives Bellota Text its odd, commanding presence. Bellota Text is best at open, unshaded letterforms, whereas Spectral does bookish text with stems slightly heavier than its crossbars.

gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-graduate: Bruno Ace draws every line like it was run along a ruler, with counters that stay open to the outside. Graduate, a serif with generous spacing between letters, reads dignified and unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-line-seed-jp: LINE Seed JP reads friendly and straightforward, its counters easy to slip in and out of. Bruno Ace gives it a ruler-drawn, one-character-per-beat heading, and the two stay clearly apart.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sour-gummy: Bruno Ace looks like glass tubing bent into letters. Sour Gummy, a sans with wide gaps that keep small text crisp, stays quiet beneath it and lets the heading do the talking.

gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sura: Ruler-straight and loud, Bruno Ace heads the page, with Sura, a serif, offering comfortable stroke contrast just beneath it. Paragraphs would read with a traditional, authoritative air, never rushed.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-cairo-play: Bruno Ace SC has a wire-like skeleton, spaced like beads on a thread. It excels at making a striking statement, while Cairo Play, a sans-serif with open round letters, stays legible when small.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-carme: Bruno Ace SC strings its letters out like beads on a long thread. Carme then keeps things modern and quiet, its open counters letting the stretched-out display line stay the star.

gen-gf-carme-fs-literata: Literata brings sturdy, bookish serif strokes with a faint taper, sitting under Carme, whose clean lines never show a hairline. Bookish warmth against crisp contemporary clarity is the whole appeal.

gen-gf-cause-fs-plein: Plein reads clear and reliable, a sans with an open channel into every round letter, under Cause, a friendly handwritten heading. Pages stay light and inviting, suited to brief text.

gen-gf-cherry-swash-gf-cardo: Cherry Swash opens its c like a horseshoe, with diagonals as heavy as the verticals. Cardo answers with a classic serif's softly varied strokes, its diagonals slightly thinner, as if gently pressed.

gen-rubik-fs-karma: Friendly is the first word for Rubik, with its big x-height and bowls that feel open and inviting. Karma follows as a classic serif with a calm modulation, so size it modestly and it stays trustworthy beside that heading.
gen-rye-fs-paquito: Authoritative and vintage, Rye stands tall with hairline-tipped stems that give its lowercase a dark, sparkling texture. And Paquito, a confident text serif, is approachable and made for a quick read.
gen-shadows-into-light-fs-hoover: Friendly and inviting, with letters crowded like chalk on a full slate. Shadows Into Light is best at casual charm, while Hoover, a robust text serif, is happiest in quick bursts.
gen-shadows-into-light-mulish: Crowded chalk-mark letters give Shadows Into Light a hand-scrawled, friendly feel. Mulish, a modern sans with unmodulated strokes, sits beside it easily, so the scrawl feels approachable rather than messy.
gen-shrikhand-fs-literata: Shrikhand brings a commanding, warm display voice with plenty of weight behind it. And Literata, a sophisticated text serif with subtly varied strokes, hushes it down to a bookish murmur.
gen-shrikhand-fs-rowan: Shrikhand has commanding, warm display letters with a low-contrast heft that grabs the eye before anything else. Rowan, a friendly literary serif, wouldn't carry pages of dense text.
gen-silkscreen-fs-ranade: Lo-fi retro letters with room to breathe all around each one. Silkscreen and Ranade both love wide spacing, and the sans-serif's organic, slightly rubbery stroke warms up the whole retro mood.
gen-silkscreen-gf-actor: Lo-fi spaghetti lines, with space you can almost feel around each letter, make Silkscreen the loud one here. Actor stays clean and modern, a quiet foil with barely curled s curves.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kiwi-maru: Space around every letter that you can almost feel defines Silkscreen, with lines like spaghetti laid out flat. Kiwi Maru, a traditional serif with generous letterspacing, gives the retro look an editorial anchor.
gen-silkscreen-gf-special-gothic: Lo-fi and retro, with room around every letter that you can nearly feel. Special Gothic does open, rounded sans-serif friendliness best, while Silkscreen brings the swagger of spaced-out spaghetti lines.
gen-space-grotesk-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with wide-mouthed curves. Space Grotesk, a geometric sans-serif cut from single-weight strokes like a flat stencil, makes that quiet stroke contrast feel much sharper.
gen-space-mono-fs-ranade: Typewriter-stiff stencil letters up top, then a loose, stretched-out line below. Ranade's gentle taper and tall lowercase soften what Space Mono draws as a rigid ribbon.
gen-space-mono-montserrat: Montserrat reads wide and gliding, with generous curves that slide past quickly. Space Mono is best at being blunt and mechanical, while Montserrat does its best work being smooth and welcoming in a plain sans way.
gen-special-elite-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro keeps its curves open and its lines crisp, like bent steel rod under a worn, smudged headline in Special Elite. Be Vietnam Pro is the steadier half, and that gap is the whole appeal.
gen-special-elite-fs-hoover: Hoover reads refined yet robust, its e opening generously and its ascenders cut short beneath distressed Special Elite. A page of it would feel steady, sturdy and never fussy at all.
gen-special-elite-fs-nunito: Special Elite brings a scuffed, typewritten look with a wide-mouthed a, while Nunito's big round bowls and open endings take over below. Pages of it should feel friendly and easy going.
gen-special-elite-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tight, with big counters and curves that refuse to close, a warm plain sans under the headline. And Special Elite's distressed, tall-filling lowercase stands out best when it is sized well above it.
gen-special-elite-fs-trench-slab: Worn and typewritten, Special Elite fills the line with oversized lowercase, and Trench Slab sits under it, dignified and compact. One does rough character best; the other does refined structure.
gen-special-elite-montserrat: Distressed and a bit rebellious, Special Elite fills each line with its wide-mouthed a. Montserrat is the smooth foil, with its wire-like glide, where the headline is gritty and knocked about.
gen-special-elite-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads precise and structured, its middle zone dominating the line with open throats on a, c, e and s. Against Special Elite's distressed look, the structure becomes the pair's best quality.
gen-syne-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Syne's x-height climbs almost to cap height, giving headlines a bold, experimental stripe of constant ink. And Be Vietnam Pro follows with open curves and a high mean line that read cleanly.
gen-syne-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab is grounded, refined, and tall in every lowercase letter. Syne is best at commanding, experimental display, all bent-wire strokes, while the text serif quietly handles the refined reading.
gen-syne-fs-hoover: Syne draws a smooth, pinch-free line with no swell where its curves turn corners. And Hoover, refined and robust, reads steadily over time, its generous e openings and compressed ascenders keeping lines tight and sturdy.
gen-syne-fs-paquito: Syne has the steadiness of a drawn string, experimental and commanding at once. And Paquito, confident and approachable, sits quietly beneath with almost no gap between its lowercase and caps, so the two settle together easily.
gen-syne-fs-quicksand: Experimental from the first letter, Syne draws smooth, pinch-free curves. Syne is best at commanding, tall-x-height display lines, while Quicksand is best at approachable text with bulb-like bowls and open stroke ends.
gen-syne-fs-ranade: Experimental Syne keeps the arches of its r, n and m closely matched to their stems. And Ranade, gently shifting in weight with widely spaced letters, looks best given a little extra size.
gen-syne-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified and refined, its lowercase standing nearly level with the capitals. And Syne is best at a bold, followable outline of constant width, while the body is best at quiet, steady text.
gen-syne-gf-graduate: Smooth as bent wire, Syne leads, then Graduate follows, bookish and dignified, with generous white between its letters. Syne is best at bold display punch; Graduate at quiet, steady text.
gen-titan-one-fs-asap: Titan One is bold and playful, built from tube-like, constant-weight strokes. Asap works nicely at a modest size under big headings, its open c arcs and near-capital body height staying easy to follow.
gen-titan-one-fs-public-sans: Titan One has tubelike, constant-weight lines with stems and arcs in lockstep, bold and playful. Public Sans then settles into a hefty, trustworthy lowercase, with broad counters that keep paragraphs feeling open and steady.
gen-titan-one-inter: Inter keeps its lines smooth and open, like a tube cut clean. Under Titan One's chunky, brush-ended curves, a longer read goes down easily, with big counters and tall lowercase doing the work.
gen-titan-one-montserrat: Titan One stamps out chunky letters with a towering midzone and curves that stop like lifted brush strokes. Montserrat follows in a sans that glides under the eye, so a longer read feels spacious and friendly.
gen-titan-one-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its lowercase looking big beside the capitals and its round letters holding up small. Shrink Titan One's heading down, though, and its constant, heavy line width starts to clog.
gen-tourney-fs-alpino: Cozy and casual, Alpino sits low and tall-bodied, so its ascenders look short and its curve endings stay well apart. Tourney, meanwhile, earns its keep when big and brief, stretching bulky letters across wide tracking.
gen-tourney-fs-karma: Tourney cuts every stroke with a pen that never changes pressure or angle. That suits loud, wide display lines, while Karma's gentle swell in each bowl and unhurried terminals suit sustained reading.
gen-tourney-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One reads literary and authoritative, slowing the eye to a leisurely walk with curvy, unclamped letters. Tourney is the shouter here, best when its wide-tracked, single-width strokes go big, while BhuTuka rewards lingering.
gen-tourney-gf-cascadia-code: Tourney stretches bold, athletic letters wide, every stroke cut to one width, and it's at its best loud. Cascadia Code is the opposite: a wire-like monoline with generous gaps, made for steady reading.
gen-tourney-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Wide-tracked and athletic, Tourney cuts every stroke to one width. Mochiy Pop One runs text with very large lowercase eyes, letters hung like clothespins on a line, giving a neutral, professional feel.
gen-tourney-gf-open-sans: Tourney glows like neon glass, bold and athletic. Open Sans gives it a smooth, contemporary body with bulky lowercase proportions, so give the heading plenty of space to stretch out.
gen-tourney-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, its curves turning corners without any pressure swell and its c and s held well apart. And if Tourney's heavy, wide-tracked heading gets made small, its bulky letters crowd quickly.
gen-tourney-space-grotesk: Tourney shouts in wide-tracked, bulky letters, every stroke cut to one width. Space Grotesk follows in geometric sans with a moderate lowercase and counters that breathe, so paragraphs move along without any shouting of their own.
gen-ultra-archivo: Archivo opens its curves outward with a commanding x-height, giving text an approachable, editorial footing under the heading. Ultra does the dignified vintage work, with its mellow modulation; Archivo does the plain talking.
gen-ultra-fs-bespoke-sans: Dignified and vintage, Ultra packs its letters close with only a slight swell in each bowl. But Bespoke Sans, sharp and refined, leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, so text reads freely.
gen-ultra-fs-public-sans: Ultra looks dignified and a bit vintage, with stems that outweigh its hairlines and a mild taper at every bend. Public Sans, a plain sans with a hefty lowercase, keeps long reading easy.
gen-ultra-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width, with counters that breathe, set under Ultra's close-packed serif. Over a long passage, that plain sans stays quietly geometric.
gen-unbounded-fs-fira-sans: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide, with a c that opens broadly and friendly. Fira Sans, with a larger-than-usual x-height and no thick-thin contrast, carries a long passage cleanly.
gen-unbounded-fs-gambetta: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide, with a welcoming c. That heading does friendly, contemporary display best, while Gambetta does bookish grace best, its stroke weight shifting noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-unbounded-fs-hoover: Friendly and wide-set, Unbounded sprawls across the line with oversized lowercase. Hoover, a serif with compressed ascenders and a generous opening into the e, keeps paragraph after paragraph feeling sturdy and refined.
gen-unbounded-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and clearly opening e making words easy to catch. Its plain sans solidity under Unbounded's broad, friendly display letters is the pair's best quality.
gen-unbounded-fs-ranade: Friendly through and through, Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide and opens every c with a broad welcome. Ranade's slight rubber-cord weight shifts are the quality that sets it apart.
gen-unbounded-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab reads dignified, with rounded tall letters and gaping c shapes. Unbounded sits above it as the friendly, wide-stretched display voice, and that bold swap in character is the pair's real hook.
gen-unbounded-source-serif-4: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide and friendly across the top. Source Serif 4 follows as a text serif with a slight tightening at curve tops, which would keep paragraphs moving smoothly and soberly.
gen-unbounded-switzer: Switzer reads like wire bent into letters, tall and approachable. Beneath Unbounded's broad, stretched-out display forms, a long passage would feel light and tidy, with c tips that never crowd each other.
gen-unifrakturmaguntia-fs-public-sans: Gothic and tightly clustered, UnifrakturMaguntia towers over every word. Public Sans, a sans-serif with hefty lowercase and broad open counters, keeps text that runs for pages feeling steady and trustworthy.
gen-vast-shadow-bitter: Every stroke in Vast Shadow is cut to one width, with no thin hairlines anywhere. Bitter, a slab-serif with big lowercase eyes and see-through s shapes, grounds that vintage flash so the two sit comfortably on the page.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro reads clean, its strokes like bent steel rod and its curve endings keeping their distance. Vast Shadow, with its vintage, tall-ceilinged letters, probably wants the larger size while this sans-serif stays modest below.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-familjen-grotesk: Vintage and showy, Vast Shadow has no hairlines, only uniform stems. Familjen Grotesk, a lively sans whose lowercase stands tall and whose bowls stay unfinished on one side, loosens up the heading's solid stems.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-karma: Karma keeps its terminals well clear of the stem and its thick-thin shifts quiet. Vast Shadow's curves never thin at the turns, so beside this classic serif the heading feels bolder and the text more settled.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Vast Shadow draws attention with its tall, vintage letters, each stroke cut to one width and spaced generously. Pilcrow Rounded does the quieter work, with big counters, warm curves and tight spacing that make text feel snug.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, forming a heavy-looking band of text with letters held open rather than curled shut. Vast Shadow's thin, tube-like strokes give it a vintage lift, so a larger heading size would let each one show.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-savate: Eye-catching and vintage, Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to one width with round letters as heavy as straight ones. Savate, a sans with sturdy hairlines and open curves, adds light contrast beneath.
gen-vast-shadow-mulish: Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to a single width and leaves generous space around each letter, a vintage, eye-catching look. Mulish then reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph, its open curves never snagging.
gen-vast-shadow-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads in a precise, structured way, its slab-serif middle zone dominating the line. And down the page, Vast Shadow's rope-like vintage strokes above make that steady texture feel all the more grounded.
gen-work-sans-fs-erode: Bent tubing meets editorial dignity, with Work Sans holding a single gauge through every curve. Work Sans is best at crisp open curves, but Erode is best at a gentle ebb and flow of weight.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-chillax: Fat round bowls attach to the stem by hairline joins in Yeseva One, vintage and bookish. Chillax draws a spaghetti-like line, smooth as pen-plotter ink and relaxed enough to keep reading.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-literata: Literata reads like a sophisticated serif, its thin lines sturdy and its thicker ones only slightly heavier, with wide-open curves. Under Yeseva One's snagging fat stems, that text flows gently.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy and hefty, Public Sans lays down a solid sans body with broad, open counters beneath Yeseva One's fat bowls. Swollen stems and needle-thin joins up top, sturdy low-contrast strokes below.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-roundo: Fat round bowls on hairline joins make Yeseva One the dramatic, vintage half of the pair. And Roundo, cut like a fixed-width router bit, does the quieter work of keeping small counters unclogged.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-synonym: Yeseva One gives each letter a heavy trunk and whisper-thin branches. Synonym, a sans-serif drawn with technical-pen steadiness, lays a constant-ink stripe beneath, its generous curve openings keeping that bookish drama in check.
gen-yeseva-one-sora: Sora moves with a blunt round-tip marker feel, its c and s staying widely parted at every turn. That blunt marker against Yeseva One's rope-thick stems is the real draw.
gen-young-serif-fs-bespoke-sans: Young Serif looks plain and friendly, refined without any fuss. Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, and that sharp, refined body is what makes the pairing work.
gen-young-serif-fs-roundo: Roundo reads neutral and geometric, every small counter left unclogged. Young Serif brings the refined, friendly serif shapes above, while Roundo's sans runs as a plain stripe of constant ink beneath.
gen-yuji-mai-fs-rowan: Tight-lipped and measured, Yuji Mai spaces each word out with openings so slight the letters feel nearly sealed. And Rowan opens every curve wide, literary and friendly, a face to sip rather than gulp.
gen-zen-dots-clash-grotesk: The body text reads clean and approachable, as if drawn with a fixed-width nib. Clash Grotesk carries the running text, while Zen Dots, with lots of room around each letter, owns the tech-flavored attention up top.
gen-zen-dots-fs-alpino: Zen Dots gives every letter lots of room, a tech-flavored but friendly display voice. But Alpino, cozy and casual, stands much taller in the lowercase, with curve endings kept well apart.
gen-zen-dots-fs-asap: Zen Dots is tech-flavored and friendly, with room around each letter. Asap, a sans-serif whose c forms read as open arcs and whose body height nearly matches the capitals, gives the heading a readable partner.
gen-zen-dots-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Lots of room surrounds every Zen Dots letter, whatever the weight. Be Vietnam Pro, strokes like bent steel rod and a high mean line, keeps pages of text moving smoothly, curve endings never touching.
gen-zen-dots-gf-faculty-glyphic: Faculty Glyphic is a modern, professional sans-serif with clear openings in its rounded letters. And Zen Dots supplies the display character, tech-flavored and friendly, with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans is a modern, precise sans built from monoline strokes, curve endings kept well apart. Zen Dots above, tech-flavored and friendly, loosens things up with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-sora: Zen Dots leaves lots of room around every letter, with openings that stay generous at every weight. Sora takes over with precise, geometric strokes like neon glass, no swell at the corners.
gen-zodiak-cabin: Zodiak's strokes swing hard from heavy to hairline. Cabin sits beneath it like bent tubing, a warm sans with open endings that carry you down a long page without any fuss.
gen-zodiak-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Dramatic strokes up top, a tall lowercase below. Zodiak is at its best when thick stems meet hairlines, while Be Vietnam Pro does its best work with smooth, rod-like curves that stay well apart.
gen-zodiak-fs-public-sans: Public Sans sets a hefty lowercase with broad, open counters, solid and straightforward. And Zodiak excels at dramatic stem-and-hairline swings, whereas Public Sans thrives on trustworthy, plainly drawn text.
gen-zodiak-fs-quicksand: Heavy strokes and hairlines share every Zodiak letter, which gives it an authoritative air. And Quicksand, a plain sans with bulb-round bowls and uniform bars, makes that drama feel friendly instead of stern.
gen-zodiak-fs-ranade: Zodiak brings dignified authority, its strokes swinging hard from fat to hairline. Ranade moves in with weight that shifts only slightly and stroke ends set far apart, giving each line an organic, spread-out feel.
gen-zodiak-fs-synonym: Zodiak sets bold stems against hairline counterparts, whereas Synonym keeps stencil-cut letters at a constant width with generous curve openings. That clash of dramatic modulation and dependable plainness is the draw.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-giga: Zodiak arrives stately, its strokes swinging hard from heavy to fine. Lexend Giga, a sans with flat linework and wide tracking, lets each word open up, so extended text moves at a slow, measured pace.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-tera: Zodiak packs heavy stems and thread-thin hairlines into each letter, while Lexend Tera plots every stroke to a single measured width. Text feels spaced out, a stepping-stone stroll across the page.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-zetta: Heavy stems framed by hairline strokes give Zodiak its dignified, authoritative bite. And Lexend Zetta runs wide and tall-bodied in a sans-serif of constant width, so a long page moves along smoothly, unhurried and open.
gen-zodiak-gf-orbit: Sharp edges, weighty stems, razor-thin arcs: that is Zodiak. Orbit, a sans-serif with curves that stop short and letters floating apart, gives the heading a rope-like, pulse-free partner to push against.
gen-zodiak-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, with big counters. Zodiak does bold stems and razor-thin horizontals best, while Inter's horizontals match its verticals, which keeps text steady and easy to follow.
gen-zodiak-mulish: Thick downstrokes sit beside hairline crossbars in Zodiak, a serif with real authority. Mulish follows in a plain sans with large, modern shapes and uniform strokes, so a long page feels friendly and unfussy.
gen-zodiak-sora: Sora is precise and geometric, with a constant stroke. Its plain sans lines have no pressure swell at the curves, which gives Zodiak's swelling, hairline-tapering stems a sharp, dignified foil.
gen-zodiak-work-sans: Work Sans draws a plain unmodulated outline with c tips held well apart, while Zodiak pairs fat stems with razor-thin hairlines. Long text moves along in a modern, unfussy way.
ibm-plex-serif-ibm-plex-sans: IBM Plex Serif has a literary, authoritative voice, with gentle weight shifts along each curve (fine for, say, a birthday invitation). IBM Plex Sans takes over as a technical, approachable sans-serif with a wide channel into every bowl.
jetbrains-mono-inter: Developer-minded and contemporary, JetBrains Mono sets fixed-width, loosely strung characters whose terminals stay open like scissor blades. Inter then carries the text as a smooth sans-serif, its big counters and tall lowercase making a long stretch glide by.
josefin-cabin: Precise, wire-cut letters from Josefin Sans sit low, while Cabin's bent-tubing curves feel warmer, say, in an empty state illustration. Low lowercase up top, a taller, friendlier body below.
libre-baskerville-manrope: Wide, loose and dignified, with authority to spare. Libre Baskerville spaces its letters generously, and Manrope's bright curve openings and steady pen line give a sans-serif that stays approachable.
lora-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans has soft, open-mouthed curves in its small letters. Lora takes the heading as a serif with authority, its thin strokes only slightly lighter than the thick ones, wide-mouthed on round forms.
merriweather-poppins: Dignified serif sturdiness up top, with rope-loose sans curves underneath it. Merriweather does best with mid-level stroke contrast and sturdy bowls, while Poppins does best at uniform, strip-cut lines with a tall body.
montserrat-merriweather: Montserrat draws a thread of ink with no swelling, stays crisp when shrunk, and stands in a tall central band. Merriweather does cozy best, with a stocky line and soft modulation.
playfair-inter: Dignified from the first glance, Playfair Display pits hairlines against fat strokes. It earns its keep big and short, while Inter keeps smooth, tube-like lines and big counters out of the way.
quilon-switzer: Editorial swagger from Quilon, in a gentle ebb and flow of stroke. Switzer's tubular, unshaded lines then carry the text, so pages of it read smoothly, friendly and never swelling.
raleway-source-serif: Source Serif 4 reads dignified, with a gaping c and bowls that thin gently at the curve tops. Raleway's wire-like line glides above it, so the serif body feels anchored beneath a lighter, precise heading.
sentient-satoshi: Tight, crisp serif forms up top, open sans letters below. Sentient's round shapes hold light back, and Satoshi lets it in through open curves, so the two trade tightness for openness.
space-grotesk-inter: Clean, geometric Space Grotesk traces its lines like one marker tip, with s terminals kept clear. And Inter, tall in the lowercase with breathing counters, feels smoother and a step taller beside it.
special-elite-dm-sans: DM Sans reads friendly and approachable, its wide-set s terminals keeping things easy going. And Special Elite pushes back with a distressed, tall x-height that fills the line, the sort of look a dj name logo might borrow.
syne-general-sans: Syne's x-height climbs almost to cap height, drawn as a plain stripe of constant ink with no pinched curves. General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure and the same tall, line-filling x-height, so the sans-serif body follows smoothly behind.
young-serif-inter: Inter reads like a smooth tube, its big counters hollow and open. Young Serif brings a friendly, refined serif voice with low contrast, and beside Inter's rope-like uniformity it feels warmer and more lived in.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-actor: Actor reads modern and tidy, with wide s curves barely curling in. Bellota's strokes all share one stylus width and its s ends hang far from the spine, which is where the pull comes from.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-graduate: Hanging s ends and stylus-width strokes mark Bellota out right away. Graduate, a serif with generous spacing and no contrast between stems and joins, brings a bookish, dignified steadiness underneath.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-: Distinctive at first glance, Bellota traces every stroke at stylus width, no brush swell. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation, a sans-serif, does the clean, modern part, its terminals stopping far from the stem.
gen-gf-bellota-plus-jakarta-sans: Distinctive up top, Bellota hangs its s ends far from the spine and traces every stroke at stylus width. Plus Jakarta Sans runs on precisely, monoline with curve endings held well apart.
gen-gf-bellota-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, its curves turning corners with no pressure swell and its c and s held widely apart. Paragraphs move along crisply, with Bellota's hanging s ends flavoring the top.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-familjen-grotesk: Open shapes, no shading: Bellota Text stays smooth and plain while Familjen Grotesk leaves its bowls unfinished on one side. Familjen's taller lowercase moves with a livelier stride than the heading's moderate one.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-ranade: Ranade reads organic and composed, its weight shifting only slightly like stretched rubber cord, stroke ends set far apart. Bellota Text, by contrast, keeps horizontals matching verticals in thickness.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-roundo: Bellota Text opens its curves wide and skips calligraphic shading entirely. Roundo, a sans whose n has arch and stem matching, keeps small counters unclogged under that shading-free heading.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-actor: Wire-cut strokes and open curves give Bellota Text a sharp look. Bellota Text does the attention-grabbing; Actor, a sans with wide s curves barely curled in, does the modern, clean reading.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-brawler: Bellota Text matches its diagonals to its stems and leaves its curves open, free of any calligraphic shading. Brawler's softly varied strokes add a literary, refined warmth to the text.
